name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=pathfind, descriptor=recursive_with_direction). Accurately describes the routine: a recursive 4-neighbour pathfind expander that tags each visit with a direction code. No Ghidra address residue in the name; no domain ID to preserve. Confirmed by disasm (INC/DEC depth marker, right/left/down/up branches each setting a direction byte) and by the single caller fd2_pathfind_to_destination.
purpose: Direction-tracked recursive pathfind expansion: visits the four neighbours (right/left/down/up) of the current tile, tags each with a direction code into the step-stack frame, and recurses into any neighbour whose cost step improved, so the orchestrator can reconstruct the chosen path.
logic_summary: Pushes this level's 8-byte frame {x, y, cost, dir} onto data_fd2_battle_pathfind_step_stack at the current depth and increments data_fd2_battle_pathfind_current_depth (binary: write 8 bytes at EDI, INC [0x60077]). Then runs four mirror branches in order right/left/down/up, rewriting the frame's direction byte before each (3=right, 1=left, 0=down(y+1), 2=up(y-1)). Each branch bounds-checks the neighbour (right/down: unsigned (coord+1)<extent; left/up: coord!=0), calls fd2_pathfind_neighbor_step_with_tiebreak(x',y',cost,neighbour_btm,&new_cost) which returns non-zero (binary carry-clear) iff the tile improved and the search should descend, and recurses into the neighbour with the reduced new_cost on a non-zero return. x/y/cost/btm_ptr persist unchanged across all four directions and across the recursive call (binary reloads them from the saved EDI frame). Decrements data_fd2_battle_pathfind_current_depth on exit. Unlike the flood-fill twin, the step-stack frame is load-bearing data (the direction bytes are read back by the tiebreak/destination helpers), so the emit keeps the real frame writes while using native C recursion for control flow.
signature: void fd2_pathfind_recursive_with_direction(uint8 x, uint8 y, uint8 cost, uint8 *btm_ptr)

params.name: x
params.semantics: Current tile X coordinate (DL in the binary); right branch uses (x+1)<map_width, left branch requires x!=0.

params.name: y
params.semantics: Current tile Y coordinate (DH in the binary); down branch uses (y+1)<map_height, up branch requires y!=0.

params.name: cost
params.semantics: Residual movement budget left at this tile (CL in the binary); passed to the neighbour step and stored into the step-stack frame as frame[2].
params.reason: Accurate name for the residual movement budget; matches the flood-fill twin's naming.

params.name: btm_ptr
params.semantics: Pointer to this tile's marker byte in the battle tile map (EBX in the binary); neighbour offsets are +/-4 (horizontal) and +/-stride (vertical). Stored into the frame at +4 and reloaded after each branch.
params.reason: Accurate name (battle-tile-map marker pointer); consistent with the flood-fill twin's param naming. No address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value; results are side effects -- marker writes via the neighbour step and the direction byte sequence in the step stack, which downstream helpers snapshot into the path output buffer.
